result:
I'm staging this through the new-project entry, since nothing is built yet. Your brief, `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`, has no numbered requirements, so the outcomes below are candidates I took from it. Each needs your confirmation. I used the three research files only for facts and costs. No roadmap text is written yet.

## Outcome candidates (unranked, all from `ces-revisions-prompt.md`)

| # | Outcome (what you get) | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision size by stage over time for national total nonfarm, SA, at all four stages: 1st→2nd, 2nd→3rd, 3rd→benchmark, and wedge-back on intervening months | Small for the two sample-based stages: BLS publishes a total-nonfarm revisions table, which the ChatGPT file cites. Benchmark and wedge-back stages need full vintages from ALFRED (FRED API limit about 120 requests/min). Total vintage count and volume: unknown, the core stage measures it. |
| O2 | The same history by NAICS supersector | ALFRED supersector vintage coverage is unverified; measured by the core stage. |
| O3 | SA revisions split into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part | Needs NSA vintages alongside SA. Whether ALFRED holds enough NSA vintages is unknown; only fetching them can tell. |
| O4 | Whether collection interval (days from the reference week to release) and first-closing collection rate move the scale of 1st→2nd and 2nd→3rd revisions | Collection days follow from the calendar alone. BLS publishes collection-rate tables, but how far back they go is unverified. |
| O5 | A descriptive account of revision scale against BLS funding, staffing and sample size, explicitly not causal | Mostly your time: about 40 annual budget justifications to hand-extract, plus FedScope staffing counts. Hours per year of data are unknown until one year is extracted. |
| O6 | A multi-vintage state-space estimate that separates news from noise at each stage, with the benchmark as an irregular, more precise observation and wedge-back modeled | NUTS runtime is unknown until a first fit on real data. |
| O7 | Revision-scale estimates that hold up across the structural breaks (2003, 2020–22, sample redesigns) | Little marginal data cost; mainly model and compute cost on top of O6. |

## Proposed tracks

- **A — Revision vintages and descriptive history** (O1, O2). Known progression: assemble the vintages, compute revisions by stage, describe them. Every other track consumes this, so it is a dependency regardless of how you rank.
- **B — Seasonal vs. sample split** (O3). Research. Kept separate from C because the split stands whether or not collection interval matters, and joining them would make O3 wait on the collection covariates.
- **C — Collection interval** (O4). Research. It is identified from sharp within-year variation, unlike D.
- **D — Operational capacity** (O5). Research. Split from C because it uses slow, collinear annual series with a different identification problem, and it is dominated by hand-built data. C should not wait on that.
- **E — Joint Bayesian state-space model** (O6, O7). Research. The method is open. Driver effects from B, C or D can enter it later, but its news/noise answer stands without them.

Qualities like a point-in-time vintage store with manifests, full validation (PPCs, LOO against a constant-variance baseline, pseudo-real-time), and supersector hierarchy will go into later stages or Ranked-list items, never into a core stage's Exit.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 managed with uv (`.python-version`, `uv.lock`).
- Stack from the brief: NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax if needed, ArviZ, Polars.
- The estimand is revision **scale**: covariates enter the variance, not only the mean.
- Party of the appropriators is descriptive grouping only.
- One cheap check is still open: whether current JAX wheels support Python 3.14.

**Proposed roadmap name:** `ces-revisions`, written to `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. That file does not exist yet.

**Optional probe, only if you say yes:** list ALFRED's vintage dates for PAYEMS and PAYNSA (two API calls). This would firm up the cost notes for O1 and O3.

## One request

Please:

- rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves;
- confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name;
- say whether to run the probe.
